PARTIAL PROMOTION, 9 of 11 functions. The licensed run is narrowed to 0x02132dc0..0x02133254; the destructor pair at 0x02132d04 (D0) and 0x02132d6c (D1) stays in its two enrolled shards and this TU's own copies are licensed deadstrip-duplicate. Both copies BYTE-MATCH: the pre-narrowing run, with all 11 licensed, reported 11/11 MATCH, so the source form is right and only the ORDER is unreproducible. As shipped this entry licenses 9, and tubuild verify reports 9/9 MATCH.

Why the order cannot be reproduced: the cartridge puts D0 (0x02132d04) BELOW D1 (0x02132d6c). The mwccarm 2004/b56 lever set for destructor variant order is closed and measured: a destructor defined inline in the class body emits D1 then D0, always; an out-of-line definition emits D2, D0, D1 and adds a homeless D2. Scaffolds (an explicit p->~X() call, a delete p) and moving the declaration below the overrides change nothing. No admissible source form emits D0 below D1 without a D2 the ROM does not carry, so the pair cannot sit in this TU's licensed run (linkcheck [4b/8] refuses a licensed .text that is not ROM-ascending).

The inline form is also required independently: include/daDsnBase_c.h defines the destructor in the class body so that both descendants (daDsn_c in ov091, daDkk_c in ov025) INLINE the body. An out-of-line declaration would make each descendant emit a bl the ROM does not have, and would move the key function off CleanupResources.

Reachability: the only two references to either address anywhere in config/ are vtable words -- relocs.txt 0x0213523c -> 0x02132d6c and 0x02135240 -> 0x02132d04, both inside _ZTV11daDsnBase_c (0x021351fc). No instruction in the image calls either address directly, so nothing outside the vtable depends on their order.
